question.leadin: This son of Akhenaten ruled with the assistance of the vizier Ay ("eye"), who eventually succeeded him after his death.
question.text: Name this "Boy Pharaoh" of Egypt, whose tomb was famously discovered nearly intact by Howard Carter.
question.clue: This pharaoh moved Egypt's capital back to Thebes from Amarna and reinstated the worship of traditional Egyptian gods.

swap.leadin: This woman was the last ruler of the Ptolemaic [tall-uh-may-ik] dynasty.
swap.text: Name this last queen of independent Egypt before it was conquered by the Romans.
swap.clue: Drinking pearls dissolved in vinegar apocryphally won a bet for this ruler, whose short-lived successor was Caesarion.

question.leadin: This structure is the burial place for the Pharaoh Khufu.
question.text: Name this limestone structure, which is the only of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World still standing.
question.answerHtml: The Great Pyramid of Giza (Or Great Pyramid of Khufu, or Pyramid of Cheops , prompt on pyramid or The Pyramids )
question.clue: Slave labor was long thought to have been used to build this structure, but many archaeologists believe that thousands of skilled laborers were used instead over a 20 year period.

swap.text: King Tut's tomb was discovered by this man who lost many comrades, including expedition leader Lord Carnarvon, after an alleged "mummy's curse".
swap.clue: Starting at age 17, this person worked for Gaston Maspero, who provided a recommendation for a later employer.

question.leadin: Antipater of Sidon listed one of this site's structures as one of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World.
question.text: Name this site of the Great Pyramids, located just outside Cairo.
question.clue: The greatest wonders you beheld were the three pyramids of this city, the largest of which was built by the great pharaoh Khufu.

swap.text: Cleopatra VII was the final pharaoh of this kingdom, which was founded after Alexander's death by one of his generals. It was annexed by Rome in 30 BCE.

question.leadin: A unit from this city was composed of 150 pairs of male lovers.
question.text: Name this home of the Sacred Band. This city would obtain control over the Peloponnese at the Battle of Leuctra, crushing the army of Cleombrotus I.
question.clue: Troops from this city employed the "cutting off the snake's head" technique to defeat Cleombrotus of Sparta.

swap.leadin: Name some military leaders of the ancient Near East FTPE.
swap.text: A man by this name founded a kingdom in Egypt after Alexander's death. Many rulers sharing this name ruled Egypt for centuries afterwards.
swap.clue: A figure with this name explained the apparent motion of the planets using "epicycles" in the Almagest.

question.leadin: While working in this city, Eratosthenes ("eh-ra-TOSS-thuh-neez") of Cyrene produced the first known estimate of the circumference of the Earth.
question.text: Name this ancient center of learning that flourished as the capital of Ptolemaic ("toll-uh-MAY-ic") Egypt. This city's namesake Great Library and its large collection of papyrus scrolls were burned down by Julius Caesar in 48 BC.
question.clue: A Christian mob in this home city of Origen (OR-ih-jen) made a "martyr for philosophy" by killing the Neoplatonist Hypatia.

swap.text: Reuben Chase served with John Paul Jones, who eventually began to fight, in the victory of the Bonhomme Richard over this British ship commanded by Richard Pearson.

question.leadin: The word aamu may refer to these people during their early contacts.
question.text: Name these people who invaded Egypt during the Second Intermediate Period. These people, who introduced the chariot to Egypt, constituted Egypt's Fifteenth Dynasty.
question.clue: Their capital was at Avaris, and they were overthrown by Ahmose.

swap.text: Aksumite rulers were known for constructing monuments of this type, consisting of tapered pillars with a pyramidal top. Many Egyptian monuments of this type, such as ones named "Lateran" and "Vatican," were installed in Rome under the Roman Empire.
swap.clue: One of these structures built by Aksum was cut into three pieces for transport to Italy before being repatriated in 2005. A pair of these objects named for Cleopatra are found in London and New York City.

question.text: The existence of this pharaoh is attested to by a namesake palette that depicts him with two crowns. This pharaoh was the unifier of Upper and Lower Egypt.
question.clue: This pharaoh who unified Upper and Lower Egypt and is depicted on a namesake palette wearing the crowns of both parts. Alternatively, name the legendary unifier of Egypt who is often identified with him.

swap.leadin: Emperor Claudius wrote a letter to the inhabitants of a city in this province about Jewish freedom of worship.
swap.text: Name this region that became a Roman province a decade after its Queen Arsinoe was executed in Rome.
swap.clue: By the 1st century C.E. this province produced the largest share of the cura annonae.

question.text: This founder of a namesake dynasty was dubbed "Soter" by the Rhodians for helping to fend off the besieging Antigonids. Perdiccas was killed after a failed attack on this sometimes-ally, sometimes-enemy of Seleucus I.
question.answerHtml: Ptolemy I Sotēr [also accept Ptolemaios Lagides or Ptolemy, Son of Lagus; prompt on Ptolemy or Ptolemaios]
question.clue: He acquired his first wife Artacama during the mass wedding at Susa, cemented a later alliance by marrying Antipater's daughter Eurydice, and finally chose another wife, Berenice, to elevate to the title of queen.

swap.leadin: The Tjeker, Denyen, and Lukka are listed among this group, as are the Peleset, believed to be the Biblical Philistines.
swap.text: Name this group whose great defeat at the Battle of the Delta is recorded on temple inscriptions at Medinet Habu, the mortuary temple of Ramses III. They're often blamed for the "Bronze Age Collapse."
swap.clue: A confederation of them known as the Nine Bows was fought by Merneptah, and they were responsible for the fall of Ugarit.

question.text: The pyramid at el-Lahun, or Kahun, was designed for the second pharaoh of this name, who also built a great dike there. Except for its last female ruler Sobekneferu, the entire Twelfth Dynasty consisted only of pharaohs with this name or Amenemhat.
question.clue: This name of three Twelfth Dynasty pharaohs. Herodotus gave this name's Greek equivalent to a pharaoh who supposedly erected genitalia-topped columns to mock the cities he conquered in Asia Minor and Thrace.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about water in ancient Egypt.
swap.text: Two massive statues known by this name were built by Amenhotep III to stand guard over his mortuary temples at the Theban metropolis across the Nile from Luxor. Several projects have been designed around preventing the Nile from eating away at these statues.
swap.clue: These are two giant statues of the deified Amenhotep III, one of which depicts his wife Tiy and mother Mutememwia. They flank the entrance of his mortuary temple pylon across the Nile from Luxor.

question.text: Though most Egyptologists agree that ancient Egyptians were not black, they are certain that pharaohs from this dynasty were black. This last dynasty in the Third Intermediate Period lasted from 760 BC to 656 BC, and its fall marked the beginning of the Late Period.

swap.text: A reconstruction of the Scorpion Macehead depicts three standards with these symbols hanging from them by a rope. These symbols, which are under the feet of the bronze Sphinx statuette of Thutmose III, are frequently used to represent the many enemies of Egypt.
